event: Area Control Error (ACE) is defined in the early 1950s for tie-line bias control, the automatic load-frequency control method that North America has preferred ever since
source: North American Electric Reliability Corporation. "White Paper on the Calculation of Reporting ACE." November 10, 2015. https://nercstg.nerc.com/pa/Stand/Project%2020101421%20Phase%202%20DL/White_Paper_on_the_Calculation_of_Reporting_ACE-D4_11102015.pdf.

event: UCPTE is founded at an inaugural meeting in May 1951 (Austria, Belgium, France and West Germany among the founders) to coordinate production and transmission in continental Europe
source: ENTSO-E. "The Union for the Co-ordination of Transmission of Electricity." Former associations. https://docstore.entsoe.eu/news-events/former-associations/ucte.

event: PJM installs its first online computer for automatic generation control (an analog AGC computer); its first energy management system follows in 1968
source: PJM Interconnection. "PJM History." https://pjm.com/about-pjm/who-we-are/pjm-history.aspx.

event: The Interconnected Systems Group meets in 1962 to prepare for one large synchronised system; its Interconnection Coordination Committee recommends an informal operating organisation, adopted when NAPSIC forms in January 1963 and issues voluntary operating criteria and guides
structure: North American Power Systems Interconnection Committee (NAPSIC)
source: North American Electric Reliability Corporation. "NERC Timeline." March 2023. https://www.nerc.com/news/Documents/March%202023%20NERC%20Timeline.pdf.

event: Northeast blackout (9 November 1965) leaves about 30 million people in the northeastern US and southeastern Ontario without power
source: North American Electric Reliability Corporation. "NERC Timeline." March 2023. https://www.nerc.com/news/Documents/March%202023%20NERC%20Timeline.pdf.

event: NPCC is formed (consistent with Recommendation 4 of the FPC blackout report) and develops criteria, guides and procedures that set compliance requirements for its members
source: Hydro-Québec. "Reliability News No. 11: History of Reliability Regulation in North America." https://www.hydroquebec.com/reliability-coordinator/reliability-news/reliability-news-history-reliability-regulation-north-america.html.

event: Federal Power Commission report to the President, Prevention of Power Failures (3 vols.), recommends a council on power coordination; the proposed Electric Power Reliability Act of 1967 is not enacted
source: US Federal Power Commission. Prevention of Power Failures: An Analysis and Recommendations Pertaining to the Northeast Failure and the Reliability of U.S. Power Systems. Washington, DC, 1967. https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/001627665.

event: National Electric Reliability Council (NERC) is founded in June 1968 by twelve regional and area organisations as a voluntary body, in response to the 1965 blackout and on the FPC's recommendation
source: North American Electric Reliability Corporation. "NERC Timeline." March 2023. https://www.nerc.com/news/Documents/March%202023%20NERC%20Timeline.pdf.

event: First vendor-built EMS (Control Data Corporation) enters service at Wisconsin Electric Power; AEP had built the first US experimental state estimator; SCADA, AGC, state estimation and contingency analysis are bundled as the EMS
source: "Foreword." In Power System State Estimation (reading sample). e-bookshelf. https://content.e-bookshelf.de/media/reading/L-24020912-41fca1d3f6.pdf.

event: NAPSIC becomes part of NERC as the NERC Operating Committee, and NERC adopts NAPSIC's operating criteria and guides
source: North American Electric Reliability Corporation. "NERC Timeline." March 2023. https://www.nerc.com/news/Documents/March%202023%20NERC%20Timeline.pdf.

event: NERC's Board establishes the security coordinator function (later renamed reliability coordinator) and requires each region to file a reliability plan for Operating Committee approval
source: Renewable Energy World. "NERC News for August." 2002. https://www.renewableenergyworld.com/energy-business/policy-and-regulation/nerc-news-for-august/.

event: NERC's System Operator (Personnel) Certification Program begins on a voluntary basis (continuing education program from 2004); credentials later include Reliability Coordinator Operator and are valid for three years
source: California ISO et al. "Joint Comments in Response to NERC Petition for Approval of Proposed Revisions to Rules of Procedure, RR17-6." July 17, 2017. https://www.caiso.com/documents/jul17_2017_jointcomments-response_nercpetition_approval_proposedrevisions_rules_procedure_rr17-6.pdf.

event: CAISO's Market Surveillance Committee (chaired by Frank Wolak from 1 April 1998) acts as independent external monitor of the new California market; the internal Department of Market Analysis later becomes the Department of Market Monitoring
structure: CAISO Market Surveillance Committee; Department of Market Monitoring
source: California ISO Market Surveillance Committee. "Preliminary Report on the Operation of the Ancillary Services Markets." December 1998. https://www.caiso.com/Documents/1998121806474113564.pdf.

event: After WSCC system breakups on 2 July and 10 August 1996, WSCC adopts the Reliability Management System: members contractually accept standards, WSCC monitors compliance and imposes sanctions, appeals go to a Reliability Compliance Committee; FERC approves it on an experimental basis
structure: WSCC Reliability Management System; Reliability Compliance Committee
source: US Department of Justice. "Justice Department Will Not Challenge Western Electric Utilities Plan to Enforce Reliability Standards." Press release, 1999. https://www.justice.gov/archive/atr/public/press_releases/1999/2497.htm.

event: FERC Order 2000 (December 1999), building on Order 888's 1996 ISO principles, lists market monitoring among the minimum functions of a Regional Transmission Organization
source: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. "Regional Transmission Organizations." Federal Register 65, no. 46 (March 8, 2000). https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2000-03-08/pdf/00-5021.pdf.

event: NERC moves from a stakeholder board to a fully independent Board of Trustees advised by a stakeholder committee, proposed by the same task force that proposed mandatory, enforceable standards
source: Popowsky, Sonny. Testimony before the Senate Committee on Governmental Affairs. June 28, 2001. https://www.hsgac.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/imo/media/doc/062801popowsky.pdf.

event: NERC applies for ANSI accreditation of its standards development process (process manual for Board approval on 14 June 2002); a Standards Committee authorises standard requests and appoints drafting teams
structure: NERC Standards Committee; ANSI-accredited standards process
source: North American Electric Reliability Council. "Application for ANSI Accreditation." May 2002. https://nercstg.nerc.com/pa/Stand/ANSI%20Home%20Page%20Comm/ANSI_AcreditApp0502.pdf.

event: 14 August 2003 blackout: FirstEnergy's EMS alarm function fails without operators knowing; the 2004 US-Canada Task Force report makes 46 recommendations, the first being mandatory, enforceable standards
source: US Department of Energy. "Blackout 2003: Final Implementation Report." 2006. https://www.energy.gov/oe/articles/blackout-2003-blackout-final-implementation-report.

event: NERC's Board approves blackout recommendations (February 2004); Recommendation 8a has transmission owners review zone 3 relay settings on 230 kV+ lines by 30 September 2004, with exceptions reviewed by the Planning Committee; the System Protection and Control Task Force reviews results and drafts relay loadability standard PRC-023-1 (Board-approved 12 February 2008)
structure: NERC System Protection and Control Task Force (later Subcommittee, now Working Group)
source: NERC System Protection and Control Task Force. "Zone 3 Relay Review." NERC Planning Committee, 2005. https://nercstg.nerc.com/comm/PC/System%20Protection%20and%20Control%20Subcommittee%20SPCS%20DL/Zone%203.pdf.

event: NERC Board adopts the Version 0 Reliability Standards (8 February 2005), turning operating policies and planning standards into one set under the ANSI process; PER-004-0 sets reliability coordinator staffing
source: North American Electric Reliability Corporation. "Version 0 Reliability Standards." https://www.nerc.com/pa/Stand/Pages/Version-0.aspx.

event: UCTE Operation Handbook policies become binding among TSOs through a Multilateral Agreement in force from 1 July 2005; Policy 8 on operator training is completed at the end of 2007
structure: UCTE Operation Handbook and Multilateral Agreement
source: UCTE. "Final Report: System Disturbance on 4 November 2006." January 2007. https://www.cre.fr/fileadmin/Documents/Communiques_de_presse/import/1172593700898.pdf.

event: A Texas statute creates the ERCOT Independent Market Monitor (a contract held by Potomac Economics) to find market conduct or rules that harm efficiency or distort outcomes
source: KUT. "Texas Power Grid Watchdog Steps Down." November 9, 2023. https://www.kut.org/energy-environment/2023-11-09/ercot-texas-power-grid-watchdog.

event: The Energy Policy Act of 2005 adds FPA section 215; FERC Order 672 (3 February 2006) sets the ERO rules, and on 20 July 2006 FERC certifies NERC as the Electric Reliability Organization
source: North American Electric Reliability Corporation. "Authorities under which NERC Operates." https://nerc.com/FilingsOrders/Pages/default.aspx.

event: FERC Order 693 (March 2007) approves 83 standards, enforceable from 18 June 2007, including PER-003 (operators must hold NERC certification), so operator certification becomes mandatory
source: Troutman Pepper. "The Brief History of Mandatory Reliability Standards." https://www.troutman.com/insights/the-brief-history-of-mandatory-reliability-standards/.

event: Regional Entity delegation agreements take effect on 5 June 2007: eight Regional Entities run NERC's Compliance Monitoring and Enforcement Program (audits, alleged violations, penalties reviewed by NERC's Board Compliance Committee)
structure: Regional Entities' Compliance Monitoring and Enforcement Program (CMEP)
source: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. "Guidance Order on Reliability Notices of Penalty." Docket AD08-10-000, July 3, 2008. https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-05/20080703131349-AD08-10-000.pdf.

event: FERC creates the Office of Electric Reliability (26 September 2007), about 55 staff, director Joseph McClelland, to oversee standards development and compliance
source: FMLink. "FERC Creates Office of Electric Reliability." 2007. https://www.fmlink.com/ferc-creates-office-of-electric-reliability/.

event: FERC Order 706 (January 2008) approves CIP-002 to CIP-009; CIP-003 requires each entity to assign a single senior manager with overall responsibility and authority for CIP compliance (later the CIP Senior Manager), extended to entities without critical assets from 1 April 2010
source: White & Case. "NERC Case Notes: Reliability Standard CIP-003-1." https://www.whitecase.com/nerc-cip-003-1.

event: Florida blackout (26 February 2008): an FPL field engineer disables two levels of relay protection without authorisation or telling the load dispatcher; 22 lines, 4,300 MW of generation and 3,650 MW of load are lost
source: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. "Order Approving Stipulation and Consent Agreement, Florida Power & Light Co." Docket IN08-5-000, October 8, 2009. https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-05/20091008102212-IN08-5-0001.pdf.

event: FERC Order 719 (October 2008) requires each RTO/ISO to give its Market Monitoring Unit data, resources and personnel; Monitoring Analytics is formed on 1 August 2008 as PJM's Independent Market Monitor
structure: RTO/ISO Market Monitoring Units; PJM Independent Market Monitor
source: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. "Order on Compliance Filing, New York Independent System Operator (Order No. 719)." November 20, 2009. https://www.nyiso.com/documents/20142/1397422/FERC_Ordr_NYISO_Cmplnc_Flng_Ordr_719_11_20_09.pdf/7b2b344d-75e8-b2c7-4032-a5abf5c42993.

event: FERC Policy Statement on Compliance (16 October 2008) credits senior-management leadership, prevention, prompt detection and self-reporting, and remediation; internal compliance staff come to report high in the organisation with independent access to the CEO or board (for example CAISO's Chief Compliance Officer)
structure: Internal compliance program; chief compliance officer
source: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. "Policy Statement on Compliance." Docket PL09-1-000, October 16, 2008. https://ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-04/M-1_27.pdf.

event: FERC approves a $25 million settlement with FPL over the 2008 blackout, the largest reliability penalty since 2007; FRCC, the reliability coordinator, pays $350,000 in 2010
source: Troutman Energy Report. "FPL Accepts Largest Penalty Ever for Reliability Rules Violations." October 2009. https://www.troutmanenergyreport.com/2009/10/fpl-accepts-largest-penalty-ever-for-reliability-rules-violations/.

event: ENTSO-E (founded December 2008 by 42 TSOs) becomes operational on 1 July 2009 under Third Energy Package Regulation 714/2009; UCTE is wound up and its operational tasks transferred
source: ENTSO-E. "The Union for the Co-ordination of Transmission of Electricity." Former associations. https://docstore.entsoe.eu/news-events/former-associations/ucte.

event: NERC's event analysis process logs reportable events from October 2010, including EMS/SCADA outages of 30 minutes or more; by 2013 an EMS Task Force has reviewed 63 EMS events, and loss of monitoring or control (including AGC) becomes Category 1h in October 2013
structure: NERC Event Analysis Process; Event Analysis Subcommittee; EMS Task Force
source: NERC Event Analysis Subcommittee. "Response to Request for Research." May 10, 2013. https://nercstg.nerc.com/pa/Stand/PER%20Informal%20Development/NERC%20Event%20Analysis%20Subcommittee%20Response%20to%20Request%20for%20Research%20Updated%2010%20May%202013.pdf.

event: Arizona-Southern California outage (8 September 2011): the FERC-NERC report (May 2012) finds the system was run in an unsecured state with poor observability and awareness, and makes 27 recommendations
source: North American Electric Reliability Corporation. "FERC, NERC Release Report on 2011 Southwest Blackout." News release, May 1, 2012. https://www.nerc.com/pa/rrm/ea/September%202011%20Southwest%20Blackout%20Event%20Document%20L/PR_AZOutage01MAY12_News_Release.pdf.

event: NERC's Protection System Misoperations Task Force finds relay setting errors a leading cause of misoperations and promotes settings review; NERC has no plans to make peer review mandatory
structure: NERC Protection System Misoperations Task Force; settings peer review
source: NERC Protection System Misoperations Task Force. "PSMTF Webinar." May 7, 2013. https://nerc.com/pa/RAPA/webinardl/PSMTF_Webinar_Slides_20130507d.pdf.

event: CAISO asks FERC for a waiver to correct congestion prices after a wind-imbalance market software defect in early 2013 (about $6.6 million); it later publishes price-correction reports and routes software changes through BPM change management
structure: CAISO price-correction process; BPM change management
source: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. "Order Granting Tariff Waiver, California Independent System Operator Corp." Docket ER14-1318, May 12, 2014. https://www.caiso.com/Documents/May12_2014_OrderGrantingTariffWaiverPetition_PriceCorrections_ER14-1318.pdf.

event: FERC gives final approval (12 February 2014) to split WECC: the reliability coordinator function moves to Peak Reliability, mainly to end the conflict with WECC's enforcement role; in 2015 WECC pays a $16 million penalty over the 2011 blackout
source: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. "Order Approving Stipulation and Consent Agreement, Western Electricity Coordinating Council." Docket IN14-11-000, May 26, 2015. https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-05/IN14-11-000.pdf.

event: FERC Order 796 (20 March 2014) approves MOD-025-2, MOD-026-1, MOD-027-1, PRC-019-1 and PRC-024-1: generator owners must verify excitation and governor control models and coordinate voltage-regulator and protection settings
structure: Generator model and settings verification (generator owner, transmission planner)
source: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. "Generator Verification Reliability Standards, Order No. 796." March 20, 2014. https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-05/E-4_18.pdf.

event: ACER approves ENTSO-E's Incident Classification Scale methodology (19 September 2014); annual ICS reports classify transmission incidents, the first (for 2013) published in December 2014
source: ENTSO-E. "Incident Classification Scale Annual Report 2014." November 5, 2015. https://eepublicdownloads.entsoe.eu/clean-documents/SOC%20documents/Incident_Classification_Scale/151221_ENTSO-E_ICS_Annual_Report_2014.pdf.

event: PRC-012-2 (Board adoption November 2015) replaces the regional special protection system standards: the reliability coordinator reviews each new or changed remedial action scheme, the transmission planner re-evaluates it every 60 months, and WECC's RAS Review Subcommittee helps the RCs
structure: Reliability coordinator RAS review; WECC Remedial Action Scheme Review Subcommittee
source: North American Electric Reliability Corporation. "Project 2010-05.3 Remedial Action Schemes: Question and Answer." November 23, 2015. https://nerc.com/pa/Stand/Prjct201005_3RmdialActnSchmsPhase3ofPrtctnSystmsDL/2010-05_3_RAS_Question_Answer_redline_11232015_final.pdf.

event: MIDAS replaces webCDMS (1 July 2016) for quarterly protection-system misoperation reporting under a Section 1600 data request, after PRC-004 drops its reporting requirement
source: Midwest Reliability Organization. "PRC-004-5 Standard Application Guide." https://www.mro.net/document/prc-004-5-standard-application-guide/?download.

event: After the Blue Cut fire (16 August 2016) trips about 1,200 MW of solar PV (inverters tripping on instantaneous frequency and momentary cessation), NERC publishes its report (8 June 2017) and forms the Inverter-Based Resource Performance Task Force
structure: NERC Inverter-Based Resource Performance Task Force
source: North American Electric Reliability Corporation. "1,200 MW Fault Induced Solar Photovoltaic Resource Interruption Disturbance Report." June 2017. https://www.nerc.com/pa/rrm/ea/Documents/1200_MW_Fault_Induced_Solar_Photovoltaic_Resource_Interruption_Final.pdf.

event: EU System Operation Guideline 2017/1485 makes TSO participation in Regional Security Coordinators mandatory; Regulation 2019/943 turns them into Regional Coordination Centres with added tasks, including post-disturbance analysis
structure: Regional Security Coordinators, later Regional Coordination Centres
source: European Commission. "Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/1485 Establishing a Guideline on Electricity Transmission System Operation." https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2017/1485/data.html.

event: ISO New England board's System Planning and Reliability Committee (charter dated 2018) advises the board on system operations and on compliance with mandatory reliability standards, and reviews operational metrics
structure: ISO-NE Board System Planning and Reliability Committee
source: ISO New England. "Charter of the System Planning and Reliability Committee of the Board of Directors." September 13, 2018. https://www.iso-ne.com/static-assets/documents/2018/09/2018-09-13_bod_system_planning_and_reliability_committee_of_the_board_of_directors_charter.pdf.

event: NERC's Board approves (November 2019) the Reliability and Security Technical Committee to replace the Operating, Planning and Critical Infrastructure Protection Committees; it first meets on 4 March 2020
structure: NERC Reliability and Security Technical Committee (RSTC)
source: North American Electric Reliability Corporation. "Minutes, RSTC Meeting, March 4, 2020." https://nercstg.nerc.com/comm/RSTC/AgendaHighlightsandMinutes/FINAL_Minutes_RSTC_Meeting_March_4_2020.pdf.

event: Peak Reliability stops acting as reliability coordinator (3 December 2019) after its funders back a wind-down; CAISO (RC West) and SPP take over, so the West goes from one RC to four
structure: RC West (CAISO) and SPP reliability coordinator
source: North American Electric Reliability Corporation. "Reliability Milestone Reached in Transition to Multiple Reliability Coordinators." December 2019. https://nercstg.nerc.com/news/Pages/Reliability-Milestone-Reached-in-Transition-to-Multiple-Reliability-Coordinators.aspx.

event: Texas SB 2 (June 2021), after Winter Storm Uri, replaces ERCOT's self-selected board with members chosen by a selection committee appointed by the governor and legislative leaders, and requires PUC approval of ERCOT rules; SB 3 orders weatherization standards
structure: ERCOT Board of Directors; PUCT approval of ERCOT rules
source: S&P Global. "Texas Lawmakers Pass Emergency Pricing, Weatherization, Oversight Body Changes." June 1, 2021. https://www.spglobal.com/energy/en/news-research/latest-news/electric-power/060121-texas-lawmakers-pass-emergency-pricing-weatherization-oversight-body-changes.

event: FERC Order 881 (16 December 2021) requires transmission providers to use hourly ambient-adjusted line ratings and uniquely determined emergency ratings by 12 July 2025
source: PJM Interconnection. "FERC Order 881." Operating Committee, item 10, September 12, 2024. https://ftp.pjm.com/-/media/committees-groups/committees/oc/2024/20240912/20240912-item-10---ferc-order-881.ashx.

event: FERC letter order (4 March 2022) approves FAC-011-4 and FAC-014-3, effective 1 April 2024: each reliability coordinator's SOL methodology governs how system operating limits are set; FAC-010 is retired
source: Texas Reliability Entity. "Talk with Texas RE: 2024 SOL Standards." November 2, 2023. https://texasre.org/Documents/Presentations/Talk%20with%20Texas%20RE/Talk%20with%20Texas%20RE%20-%202024%20SOL%20Standards%20-%20November%202%2C%202023.pdf.

event: FERC approves cold-weather standard EOP-012-1 (16 February 2023), following the November 2021 FERC-NERC Winter Storm Uri inquiry (28 recommendations); revised as EOP-012-2 (2024) and EOP-012-3 (September 2025)
source: Sidley Austin. "FERC Approves New Extreme Cold Weather Reliability Standards." February 22, 2023. https://energyinfrastructurepulse.sidley.com/2023/02/22/ferc-approves-new-extreme-cold-weather-reliability-standards/.

event: FERC Order 901 directs NERC to write inverter-based resource standards (after events such as Odessa, 9 May 2021, with 1,340 MW of IBR output lost), with a final milestone due 4 November 2026; FERC approves Category 2 IBR registration (27 June 2024), with compliance from May 2026
structure: IBR standards; Category 2 generator owner/operator registration
source: LexBlog. "FERC Approves NERC's Expanded Registration Requirements." September 17, 2024. https://www.lexblog.com/2024/09/17/ferc-approves-nercs-expanded-registration-requirements/.

event: After 1,500 MW of data-centre load disconnects during a 230 kV fault (July 2024), NERC forms the Large Loads Task Force (August or October 2024; sources differ)
source: North American Electric Reliability Corporation. "Large Loads" presentation. Hosted by EPRI. https://restservice.epri.com/publicattachment/98540.

event: FERC Order 909 (24 July 2025) approves PRC-029-1 ride-through requirements for inverter-based resources and PRC-024-4 for synchronous generator protection settings, with an exemption process for hardware limits
source: North American Electric Reliability Corporation. "Statement on FERC July Open Meeting." July 2025. https://www.nerc.com/news/Pages/Statement-on-FERC-July-Open-Meeting.aspx.

event: ENTSO-E Expert Panel final report (20 March 2026) on the 28 April 2025 Iberian blackout finds no single cause and calls for automated voltage management, renewables taking part in voltage control, clearer reactive-power requirements and closer TSO-DSO coordination
source: ENTSO-E. "28 April 2025 Blackout." Updated March 20, 2026. https://www.entsoe.eu/publications/blackout/9-may-2025-iberian-blackout/.

event: NERC Level 3 essential-actions alert on computational loads (4 May 2026) follows a Level 2 alert (9 September 2025) whose responses showed entities lacked processes; Level 3 alerts need Board approval and mandatory responses; NERC proposes registering computational load entities (20 MW or more at 60 kV or above)
structure: NERC Level 3 alert; proposed Computational Load Entity registration
source: North American Electric Reliability Corporation. "Level 3 Alert: Computational Load" (posted by NYSRC). May 2026. https://www.nysrc.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/NYSRC-LLWG-5-Att.-5-NERC-Level-3-Alert-1.pdf.
